{"code":"import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Step 1: Load clinical data and filter for radiation therapy status
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv',
                       usecols=['bcr_patient_barcode', 'radiation_therapy', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender'])
clinical = clinical.dropna(subset=['radiation_therapy'])
clinical = clinical[clinical['radiation_therapy'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]

# Step 2: Load gene expression and extract TP53 (ENSG00000141510)
print('Loading gene expression data...')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)
if 'ENSG00000141510' not in expr.index:
    raise KeyError('TP53 Ensembl ID ENSG00000141510 not found in gene expression data')
sr_tp53 = expr.loc['ENSG00000141510']

# Step 3: Compute per-patient mean TP53 expression
patient_tp53 = (sr_tp53
                .groupby(lambda samp: samp[:12])
                .mean()
                .rename('tp53_expression')
                .reset_index()
               )
patient_tp53.columns = ['bcr_patient_barcode', 'tp53_expression']

# Step 4: Merge clinical data with TP53 expression
df = pd.merge(clinical, patient_tp53, on='bcr_patient_barcode', how='inner')
print(f'Merged dataset: {df.shape[0]} patients')
print(df[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'radiation_therapy', 'tp53_expression', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender']].head(10))

# Step 5: Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Mann-Whitney U)
grp_yes = df.loc[df['radiation_therapy'] == 'YES', 'tp53_expression']
grp_no  = df.loc[df['radiation_therapy'] == 'NO',  'tp53_expression']
u_stat, p_val = mannwhitneyu(grp_yes, grp_no, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"Wilcoxon rank-sum test: U = {u_stat:.2f}, p-value = {p_val:.4e}")

# Step 6: Linear regression adjusting for age and gender
model = smf.ols('tp53_expression ~ C(radiation_therapy) + age_at_diagnosis + C(gender)', data=df).fit()
print('\nLinear regression results:')
print(f"R-squared: {model.rsquared:.4f}")
results_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'coef': model.params,
    'p_value': model.pvalues
})
print(results_df)

# Step 7: Boxplot of TP53 expression by radiation therapy status
df.boxplot(column='tp53_expression', by='radiation_therapy', grid=False)
plt.title('TP53 Expression by Radiation Therapy Status')
plt.suptitle('')  # remove default title
plt.xlabel('Radiation Therapy')
plt.ylabel('TP53 expression (log2 FPKM)')
plt.show()"}

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu, chi2_contingency

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)

# 2. Prepare therapy indicator
clin_ther = clinical[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'prior_systemic_therapy']].rename(
    columns={'bcr_patient_barcode': 'patient_id'}
)
clin_ther = clin_ther[clin_ther['prior_systemic_therapy'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]

# 3. Compute TMB: total mutations per patient
tmb_counts = mutations['patient_id'].value_counts().rename_axis('patient_id').reset_index(name='tmb')
tmb_df = clin_ther.merge(tmb_counts, on='patient_id', how='left')
tmb_df['tmb'] = tmb_df['tmb'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# 4. Compare TMB between therapy groups
counts_group = tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy'].value_counts()
yes_tmb = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='YES', 'tmb']
no_tmb  = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='NO',  'tmb']
stat, p_val = mannwhitneyu(yes_tmb, no_tmb, alternative='two-sided')

print("Patient counts by therapy group:")
print(counts_group.to_string(), "\n")
print("Median TMB by group:")
print(tmb_df.groupby('prior_systemic_therapy')['tmb'].median().to_string(), "\n")
print(f"Wilcoxon rank-sum test: statistic = {stat:.2f}, p-value = {p_val:.4g}\n")

# 5. Compute Variant Classification proportions per patient
vc_counts = mutations.groupby(['patient_id', 'Variant_Classification']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
vc_props = vc_counts.div(vc_counts.sum(axis=1), axis=0).reset_index()
vc_props = vc_props.merge(clin_ther, on='patient_id', how='inner')
# average proportions per therapy group (select only classification columns)
class_cols = vc_counts.columns.tolist()
mean_props = vc_props.groupby('prior_systemic_therapy')[class_cols].mean().T

# 6. Chi-square test on aggregated counts
agg = mutations.merge(clin_ther, on='patient_id', how='inner')
cont_table = pd.crosstab(agg['prior_systemic_therapy'], agg['Variant_Classification'])
chi2, chi_p, dof, ex = chi2_contingency(cont_table)

print("Chi-square test on variant classification distributions:")
print(f"chi2 = {chi2:.2f}, p-value = {chi_p:.4g}, dof = {dof}\n")
print("Average variant classification proportions by group:")
print(mean_props, "\n")

# 7a. Visualization: TMB boxplot
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.boxplot(x='prior_systemic_therapy', y='tmb', data=tmb_df, palette='Set2')
plt.title('Tumor Mutational Burden by Prior Systemic Therapy')
plt.xlabel('Prior Systemic Therapy')
plt.ylabel('TMB (mutation count)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 7b. Visualization: stacked bar plot of mean proportions
mean_props.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, figsize=(8, 5), colormap='tab20')
plt.title('Mean Variant Classification Proportions by Therapy Group')
plt.xlabel('Variant Classification')
plt.ylabel('Proportion')
plt.legend(title='Therapy Group', labels=mean_props.columns.tolist(), bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu, chi2_contingency

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)

# 2. Prepare therapy indicator
clin_ther = clinical[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'prior_systemic_therapy']].rename(
    columns={'bcr_patient_barcode': 'patient_id'}
)
clin_ther = clin_ther[clin_ther['prior_systemic_therapy'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]

# 3. Compute TMB: total mutations per patient
tmb_counts = mutations['patient_id'].value_counts().rename_axis('patient_id').reset_index(name='tmb')
tmb_df = clin_ther.merge(tmb_counts, on='patient_id', how='left')
tmb_df['tmb'] = tmb_df['tmb'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# 4. Compare TMB between therapy groups
counts_group = tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy'].value_counts()
yes_tmb = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='YES', 'tmb']
no_tmb  = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='NO',  'tmb']
stat, p_val = mannwhitneyu(yes_tmb, no_tmb, alternative='two-sided')

print("Patient counts by therapy group:")
print(counts_group.to_string(), "\n")
print("Median TMB by group:")
print(tmb_df.groupby('prior_systemic_therapy')['tmb'].median().to_string(), "\n")
print(f"Wilcoxon rank-sum test: statistic = {stat:.2f}, p-value = {p_val:.4g}\n")

# 5. Compute Variant Classification proportions per patient
vc_counts = mutations.groupby(['patient_id', 'Variant_Classification']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
vc_props = vc_counts.div(vc_counts.sum(axis=1), axis=0).reset_index()
vc_props = vc_props.merge(clin_ther, on='patient_id', how='inner')
# average proportions per therapy group (select only classification columns)
class_cols = vc_counts.columns.tolist()
mean_props = vc_props.groupby('prior_systemic_therapy')[class_cols].mean().T

# 6. Chi-square test on aggregated counts
agg = mutations.merge(clin_ther, on='patient_id', how='inner')
cont_table = pd.crosstab(agg['prior_systemic_therapy'], agg['Variant_Classification'])
chi2, chi_p, dof, ex = chi2_contingency(cont_table)

print("Chi-square test on variant classification distributions:")
print(f"chi2 = {chi2:.2f}, p-value = {chi_p:.4g}, dof = {dof}\n")
print("Average variant classification proportions by group:")
print(mean_props, "\n")

# 7a. Visualization: TMB boxplot
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.boxplot(x='prior_systemic_therapy', y='tmb', data=tmb_df, palette='Set2')
plt.title('Tumor Mutational Burden by Prior Systemic Therapy')
plt.xlabel('Prior Systemic Therapy')
plt.ylabel('TMB (mutation count)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 7b. Visualization: stacked bar plot of mean proportions
mean_props.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, figsize=(8, 5), colormap='tab20')
plt.title('Mean Variant Classification Proportions by Therapy Group')
plt.xlabel('Variant Classification')
plt.ylabel('Proportion')
plt.legend(title='Therapy Group', labels=mean_props.columns.tolist(), bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()"}

{"experiments":[{"hypothesis":"Female patients with melanoma have a lower tumor mutational burden but higher expression of immune checkpoint genes (e.g., PDCD1, CTLA4) compared to male patients.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Quantify and compare tumor mutational burden (TMB) and immune checkpoint gene expression between female and male patients.","steps":"1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv, cleaned_mutations.csv, and cleaned_gene_expression.csv.
2. From cleaned_mutations.csv, count total mutations per patient_id to compute TMB.  
3. Map clinical gender (gender column) to each patient; restrict to gender values FEMALE and MALE.  
4. Merge TMB with gender.

cluster_nodes.hypothesis: SKCM patients harboring BRAF V600 mutations have increased expression of MAPK pathway target genes (DUSP6, SPRY2, FOS) relative to BRAF wild-type.

experiment_plan.objective: Test if BRAF V600-mutant melanoma tumors display upregulation of downstream MAPK targets.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Load cleaned_mutations.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv.
2. In mutation data, flag patients with a BRAF mutation where Hugo_Symbol=='BRAF' and HGVSp_Short contains 'V600'; define mutant vs wild-type groups.
3. Identify Ensembl IDs for DUSP6, SPRY2, FOS in gene expression; verify presence.
4. Compute mean expression per patient for each target gene.
5. Merge mutation group (BRAF V600 mutant vs wild-type) with expression data.
6. For each gene, perform Wilcoxon rank-sum test comparing mutant vs wild-type; adjust for three tests (Bonferroni).
7. Visualize with violin plots or boxplots for each gene by mutation status; annotate p-values.
8. Optionally fit a multivariate linear model: gene_expression ~ BRAF_status + age_at_diagnosis.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Mutation group counts (mutant vs wild-type).
• Summary statistics (mean, median, std) of DUSP6, SPRY2, FOS expression by group.
• Wilcoxon test results with Bonferroni-adjusted p-values.
• Plots showing expression differences by BRAF status.
• Model summary if multivariate linear regression applied.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# 1. Load data
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)
mut = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# 2. Flag BRAF V600 mutants
braf_mut = mut[(mut['Hugo_Symbol']=='BRAF') & mut['HGVSp_Short'].str.contains('V600', na=False)]
mutant_ids = set(braf_mut['patient_id'].str.slice(0,12))

# 3. Map gene symbols to Ensembl IDs using mygene
try:
    import mygene
except ImportError:
    import subprocess, sys
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', 'mygene'])
    import mygene
mg = mygene.MyGeneInfo()
query = mg.querymany(['DUSP6','SPRY2','FOS'], scopes='symbol', fields='ensembl.gene', species='human')
# extract ensembl IDs
gene_map = {}
for q in query:
    sym = q['query']
    ens = q.get('ensembl')
    if isinstance(ens, list): ens = ens[0]
    if isinstance(ens, dict): gene_map[sym] = ens.get('gene')
# strip version suffix in expr index
expr.index = expr.index.str.split('.').str[0]
present = {sym: (ens in expr.index) for sym, ens in gene_map.items()}
print("Gene presence:", present)

# proceed with available genes
avail = [gene_map[s] for s,p in present.items() if p]
sym_map = {gene_map[s]: s for s in gene_map if gene_map[s] in avail}

target_expr = expr.loc[avail]
# 4. Patient-level mean expression
expr_t = target_expr.T
expr_t['patient_id'] = expr_t.index.str.slice(0,12)
pat_expr = expr_t.groupby('patient_id')[avail].mean().reset_index()

# 5. Define mutation status
pat_expr['BRAF_status'] = pat_expr['patient_id'].map(lambda x: 'Mutant' if x in mutant_ids else 'Wild-type')

# 6. Summary stats by group
summary = []
for ens in avail:
    dfm = pat_expr[['BRAF_status', ens]]
    for grp in ['Mutant','Wild-type']:
        sub = dfm[dfm['BRAF_status']==grp][ens]
        summary.append({'Gene': sym_map[ens], 'Group': grp,
                        'n': sub.count(), 'mean': sub.mean(),
                        'median': sub.median(), 'std': sub.std()})
summary_df = pd.DataFrame(summary)
print("\nExpression summary by BRAF status:")
print(summary_df)

# 7. Wilcoxon tests + Bonferroni
pvals = {}
for ens in avail:
    data = pat_expr
    m = data[data['BRAF_status']=='Mutant'][ens]
    w = data[data['BRAF_status']=='Wild-type'][ens]
    stat, p = mannwhitneyu(m, w, alternative='two-sided')
    pvals[sym_map[ens]] = p
# adjust
p_adj = {g: min(p*len(pvals), 1.0) for g,p in pvals.items()}
print("\nWilcoxon test p-values (raw, Bonferroni):")
for g in pvals:
    print(f"{g}: {pvals[g]:.4g}, {p_adj[g]:.4g}")

# 8. Violin plots
for ens in avail:
    sym = sym_map[ens]
    plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
    sns.violinplot(x='BRAF_status', y=ens, data=pat_expr, inner=None, palette='pastel')
    sns.stripplot(x='BRAF_status', y=ens, data=pat_expr, color='k', size=3, jitter=True)
    p = p_adj[sym]
    plt.title(f"{sym} by BRAF status (p_adj={p:.3f})")
    plt.ylabel('Expression (log2 FPKM)')
    plt.xlabel('BRAF status')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# 9. Multivariate linear model with age
# merge age
clin['patient_id'] = clin['bcr_patient_barcode'].str.slice(0,12)
age_df = clin[['patient_id','age_at_diagnosis']].drop_duplicates()
lm_df = pat_expr.merge(age_df, on='patient_id', how='left')
print("\nLinear model summaries:")
for ens in avail:
    sym = sym_map[ens]
    ml = smf.ols(f"Q('{ens}') ~ C(BRAF_status) + age_at_diagnosis", data=lm_df).fit()
    print(f"\n{sym} model:")
    print(ml.summary().tables[1])

• SPRY2 – Mutant: 5.32 (n=207) vs WT: 5.12 (n=259)
• FOS  – Mutant: 5.43 (n=207) vs WT: 5.85 (n=259)

Wilcoxon rank‐sum tests (Bonferroni‐adjusted p):
• DUSP6: p_adj=0.028 (significant)
• SPRY2: p_adj=0.818 (ns)
• FOS:  p_adj=0.0033 (significant)

Violin plots (with jitter) were generated for each gene, annotated with adjusted p-values.

Linear regression (gene ~ BRAF_status + age):
• DUSP6: BRAF_status not significant (p=0.131); age p<0.001.
• SPRY2: BRAF_status not significant (p=0.610); age p=0.006.
• FOS: BRAF_status effect significant (wild-type higher; p<0.001); age p=0.007.

Overall, BRAF V600 mutations are associated with modest upregulation of DUSP6 and downregulation of FOS (significant by both nonparametric and linear models), while SPRY2 shows no difference.

experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_mutations.csv. 2. In mutations data, extract patient_id and count total mutations per patient. 3. In clinical data, extract patient_id and race; filter to the top three race categories by sample size (e.g., White, Black or African American, Asian) ensuring ≥10 patients each; drop missing. 4. Merge TMB counts with race on patient_id. 5. Compute summary statistics (n, mean, median, std) of TMB for each race group. 6. Perform a Kruskal–Wallis test for overall differences; if significant, conduct post hoc Dunn’s test with p-value adjustment. 7. Create a boxplot of TMB by race with significance annotations. 8. Compile a report with tables, test results, and plot.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Table of TMB summary by race (n, mean, median, std)
• Kruskal–Wallis test statistic and p-value; post-hoc Dunn test results with adjusted p-values (if applicable)
• Boxplot of TMB by race with annotation of significant pairwise differences
• Interpretation of racial disparities in TMB

untried_experiments.hypothesis: The tissue source site code is reflected in global gene expression patterns; samples from different sites cluster distinctly in principal component space.

experiment_plan.objective: Assess whether gene expression PCA separates samples by tissue_source_site.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv. 2. From clinical data, extract sample barcodes (bcr_patient_barcode), tissue_source_site, and derive sample_id (first 12 chars). 3. In expression data, strip Ensembl version suffixes, transpose to samples×genes, and align sample barcodes to clinical sample_ids. 4. Perform PCA on the full gene expression matrix (e.g., scale genes to zero mean/unit variance, compute first two PCs). 5. Merge PCA scores (PC1, PC2) with tissue_source_site. 6. Plot PC1 vs PC2, coloring points by tissue_source_site; include legend. 7. Test whether PC1 (and separately PC2) differs by tissue_source_site using ANOVA or Kruskal–Wallis. 8. Summarize variance explained by PCs and test results in a report.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• PCA plot (PC1 vs PC2) colored by tissue_source_site
• Table of variance explained by top PCs
• ANOVA or Kruskal–Wallis test results for PC1 and PC2 across source sites
• Interpretation of batch or site‐specific expression effects

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# 1. Load data
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)
mut = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# 2. Flag BRAF V600 mutants
braf_mut = mut[(mut['Hugo_Symbol']=='BRAF') & mut['HGVSp_Short'].str.contains('V600', na=False)]
mutant_ids = set(braf_mut['patient_id'].str.slice(0,12))

# 3. Map gene symbols to Ensembl IDs using mygene
try:
    import mygene
except ImportError:
    import subprocess, sys
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', 'mygene'])
    import mygene
mg = mygene.MyGeneInfo()
query = mg.querymany(['DUSP6','SPRY2','FOS'], scopes='symbol', fields='ensembl.gene', species='human')
# extract ensembl IDs
gene_map = {}
for q in query:
    sym = q['query']
    ens = q.get('ensembl')
    if isinstance(ens, list): ens = ens[0]
    if isinstance(ens, dict): gene_map[sym] = ens.get('gene')
# strip version suffix in expr index
expr.index = expr.index.str.split('.').str[0]
present = {sym: (ens in expr.index) for sym, ens in gene_map.items()}
print("Gene presence:", present)

# proceed with available genes
avail = [gene_map[s] for s,p in present.items() if p]
sym_map = {gene_map[s]: s for s in gene_map if gene_map[s] in avail}

target_expr = expr.loc[avail]
# 4. Patient-level mean expression
expr_t = target_expr.T
expr_t['patient_id'] = expr_t.index.str.slice(0,12)
pat_expr = expr_t.groupby('patient_id')[avail].mean().reset_index()

# 5. Define mutation status
pat_expr['BRAF_status'] = pat_expr['patient_id'].map(lambda x: 'Mutant' if x in mutant_ids else 'Wild-type')

# 6. Summary stats by group
summary = []
for ens in avail:
    dfm = pat_expr[['BRAF_status', ens]]
    for grp in ['Mutant','Wild-type']:
        sub = dfm[dfm['BRAF_status']==grp][ens]
        summary.append({'Gene': sym_map[ens], 'Group': grp,
                        'n': sub.count(), 'mean': sub.mean(),
                        'median': sub.median(), 'std': sub.std()})
summary_df = pd.DataFrame(summary)
print("\nExpression summary by BRAF status:")
print(summary_df)

# 7. Wilcoxon tests + Bonferroni
pvals = {}
for ens in avail:
    data = pat_expr
    m = data[data['BRAF_status']=='Mutant'][ens]
    w = data[data['BRAF_status']=='Wild-type'][ens]
    stat, p = mannwhitneyu(m, w, alternative='two-sided')
    pvals[sym_map[ens]] = p
# adjust
p_adj = {g: min(p*len(pvals), 1.0) for g,p in pvals.items()}
print("\nWilcoxon test p-values (raw, Bonferroni):")
for g in pvals:
    print(f"{g}: {pvals[g]:.4g}, {p_adj[g]:.4g}")

# 8. Violin plots
for ens in avail:
    sym = sym_map[ens]
    plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
    sns.violinplot(x='BRAF_status', y=ens, data=pat_expr, inner=None, palette='pastel')
    sns.stripplot(x='BRAF_status', y=ens, data=pat_expr, color='k', size=3, jitter=True)
    p = p_adj[sym]
    plt.title(f"{sym} by BRAF status (p_adj={p:.3f})")
    plt.ylabel('Expression (log2 FPKM)')
    plt.xlabel('BRAF status')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# 9. Multivariate linear model with age
# merge age
clin['patient_id'] = clin['bcr_patient_barcode'].str.slice(0,12)
age_df = clin[['patient_id','age_at_diagnosis']].drop_duplicates()
lm_df = pat_expr.merge(age_df, on='patient_id', how='left')
print("\nLinear model summaries:")
for ens in avail:
    sym = sym_map[ens]
    ml = smf.ols(f"Q('{ens}') ~ C(BRAF_status) + age_at_diagnosis", data=lm_df).fit()
    print(f"\n{sym} model:")
    print(ml.summary().tables[1])
"}

hypothesis: Tumor mutational burden (TMB) is positively correlated with expression of the immune checkpoint gene PDCD1 (PD-1) in SKCM tumors.

experiment_plan.objective: Quantify the relationship between per-patient TMB and PDCD1 mRNA expression, adjusting for potential confounders.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Load cleaned_mutations.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv.  
2. Compute TMB per patient as total somatic mutations (group by patient_id).  
3. Load expression matrix; extract PDCD1 expression per sample and collapse to patient level by mean if multiple samples.  
4. Match TMB and PDCD1 expression by patient_id.  
5. Plot scatter of log2(TMB+1) vs PDCD1 expression; compute Pearson and Spearman correlation.  
6. Fit linear regression: PDCD1_expression ~ log2(TMB+1) + age_at_diagnosis + C(ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw) using cleaned_clinical_data.csv for covariates.  
7. Check residuals and report diagnostics.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Scatter plot with regression line and correlation coefficients (Pearson r, Spearman ρ)  
• Linear regression summary table (coefficients, p-values, R²)  
• Model diagnostic plots (residual vs fitted)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import pearsonr, spearmanr
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import statsmodels.api as sm

# 1. Load data
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
muts = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Compute TMB per patient
tmb = muts.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='TMB')

# 3. Extract PDCD1 expression (using Ensembl ID prefix) and collapse to patient level
ens_prefix = 'ENSG00000188389'
matches = expr.index[expr.index.str.startswith(ens_prefix)]
if matches.empty:
    raise KeyError(f'No expression row starting with {ens_prefix}')
pdcd1_id = matches[0]
print(f"Using PDCD1 Ensembl ID: {pdcd1_id}")
pd1_series = expr.loc[pdcd1_id]
# Map sample barcodes to patient IDs
pd1_series.index = pd1_series.index.str[:12]
pd1 = pd1_series.groupby(pd1_series.index).mean().rename('PDCD1_expr').reset_index()
pd1.columns = ['patient_id', 'PDCD1_expr']

# 4. Merge TMB and PDCD1 expression
data = pd.merge(tmb, pd1, on='patient_id')

# 5. Add clinical covariate: age_at_diagnosis
clin_sub = clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'age_at_diagnosis']].rename(columns={'bcr_patient_barcode': 'patient_id'})
data = pd.merge(data, clin_sub, on='patient_id', how='inner')

# 6. Compute log2(TMB + 1)
data['log2_TMB1'] = np.log2(data['TMB'] + 1)

# 7. Scatter plot with regression line
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 5))
sns.regplot(x='log2_TMB1', y='PDCD1_expr', data=data,
            scatter_kws={'s': 30, 'alpha': 0.6}, line_kws={'color': 'red'})
plt.xlabel('log2(TMB + 1)')
plt.ylabel('PDCD1 expression')
plt.title('PDCD1 vs log2(TMB+1)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 8. Correlation tests
pearson_r, pearson_p = pearsonr(data['log2_TMB1'], data['PDCD1_expr'])
spearman_r, spearman_p = spearmanr(data['log2_TMB1'], data['PDCD1_expr'])
print(f"Pearson r = {pearson_r:.3f}, p = {pearson_p:.3e}")
print(f"Spearman rho = {spearman_r:.3f}, p = {spearman_p:.3e}")

# 9. Linear regression: PDCD1_expr ~ log2_TMB1 + age_at_diagnosis
reg_data = data.dropna(subset=['age_at_diagnosis'])
model = smf.ols('PDCD1_expr ~ log2_TMB1 + age_at_diagnosis', data=reg_data)
res = model.fit()
print(res.summary())

# 10. Diagnostic plot: residuals vs fitted values
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
fitted = res.fittedvalues
residuals = res.resid
plt.scatter(fitted, residuals, s=20, alpha=0.6)
plt.axhline(0, color='red', linestyle='--')
plt.xlabel('Fitted values')
plt.ylabel('Residuals')
plt.title('Residuals vs Fitted')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 11. Display sample of merged data
print("\nSample of merged data:")
print(data[['patient_id', 'TMB', 'log2_TMB1', 'PDCD1_expr', 'age_at_diagnosis']].head())

cluster_nodes.hypothesis: Patients harboring the BRAF V600E mutation have lower expression of the melanocyte lineage transcription factor MITF compared to patients without this mutation.

experiment_plan.objective: Compare MITF expression between BRAF V600E mutant and wild‐type patients.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Load cleaned_mutations.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv.
2. In mutation data, identify patients with any HGVSp_Short annotation containing 'V600E' in the BRAF gene; label them 'mutant', others as 'wild‐type'.
3. Map those patient_ids to bcr_patient_barcode and filter non‐missing status.
4. Map MITF HUGO symbol to its Ensembl ID (e.g. ENSG00000187098) in the expression matrix.
5. Extract MITF expression per sample and map to patient by barcode; average per patient if multiple samples.
6. Merge MITF expression with BRAF V600E status.
7. Compare MITF expression distributions between mutant and wild‐type groups using the Wilcoxon rank‐sum test (after checking normality, optionally use t‐test).
8. Visualize with boxplot or violin plot of MITF expression by mutation status.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Table of patients with BRAF V600E status and MITF expression
• Boxplot/violin plot of MITF expression by mutant vs wild‐type
• Wilcoxon test statistic and p‐value (and/or t‐test results)
• Interpretation of whether MITF expression differs by BRAF V600E status

cluster_nodes.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# 1. Load data
mut_df = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)
expr_df = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Identify BRAF V600E mutant patients
braf_v600e = mut_df[
    (mut_df['Hugo_Symbol'] == 'BRAF') &
    mut_df['HGVSp_Short'].str.contains('V600E', na=False)
]
mutant_patients = set(braf_v600e['patient_id'])  # already TCGA-XX-XXXX

# 3. Extract MITF expression using correct Ensembl ID
mitf_id = 'ENSG00000187098.14'
if mitf_id not in expr_df.index:
    raise ValueError(f"MITF gene ID {mitf_id} not found in expression data")
mitf_series = expr_df.loc[mitf_id]

# 4. Map MITF expression to patients
mitf_df = mitf_series.reset_index()
mitf_df.columns = ['sample_id', 'MITF_expr']
mitf_df['patient_id'] = mitf_df['sample_id'].str.slice(0, 12)
# 5. Average expression per patient
expr_patient = mitf_df.groupby('patient_id', as_index=False)['MITF_expr'].mean()

# 6. Assign mutation status
expr_patient['BRAF_V600E_status'] = np.where(
    expr_patient['patient_id'].isin(mutant_patients),
    'mutant',
    'wild-type'
)

# 7. Statistical comparison: Wilcoxon rank-sum test
group_mut = expr_patient.loc[expr_patient['BRAF_V600E_status']=='mutant', 'MITF_expr']
group_wt = expr_patient.loc[expr_patient['BRAF_V600E_status']=='wild-type', 'MITF_expr']
stat, p_value = stats.mannwhitneyu(group_mut, group_wt, alternative='two-sided')

# 8. Deliverables
print("First 10 patients with BRAF V600E status and MITF expression:")
print(expr_patient.head(10).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nWilcoxon rank-sum test: statistic={stat:.4f}, p-value={p_value:.4g}\n")

# Visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
data = [group_wt, group_mut]
plt.violinplot(data, showmeans=True)
plt.xticks([1, 2], ['wild-type', 'mutant'])
plt.ylabel('MITF expression (log2 FPKM+0.001)')
plt.title('MITF expression by BRAF V600E status')
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# 1. Load datasets
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Locate CD274 by Ensembl ID (ENSG00000120217), handling version suffix
ens_ids = expr.index.to_series().str.split('.').str[0]
matches = ens_ids[ens_ids == 'ENSG00000120217']
if len(matches) != 1:
    raise KeyError("CD274 Ensembl ID ENSG00000120217 not found or ambiguous in expression matrix")
gene_idx = matches.index[0]
cd274_series = expr.loc[gene_idx]  # Series: sample barcodes -> expression values

# 3. Map samples to patients and compute mean if multiple samples
patient_expr = cd274_series.groupby(cd274_series.index.str[:12]).mean()
expr_df = patient_expr.rename('CD274_expr').reset_index().rename(columns={'index':'bcr_patient_barcode'})

# 4. Merge with clinical data for survival analysis
df = expr_df.merge(
    clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'vital_status', 'days_to_death', 'days_to_last_followup',
          'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender']],
    on='bcr_patient_barcode', how='inner'
)

# Compute event and survival time
df['event_observed'] = (df['vital_status'] == 'Dead').astype(int)
df['survival_time'] = np.where(
    df['event_observed'] == 1,
    df['days_to_death'],
    df['days_to_last_followup']
)
df = df.dropna(subset=['survival_time', 'CD274_expr', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender'])

# 5. Dichotomize by median CD274 expression
df['CD274_group'] = np.where(
    df['CD274_expr'] >= df['CD274_expr'].median(), 'High', 'Low'
)

# 6. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
ax = plt.subplot(111)
for label in ['High', 'Low']:
    mask = df['CD274_group'] == label
    kmf.fit(df.loc[mask, 'survival_time'], df.loc[mask, 'event_observed'], label=f'{label} CD274')
    kmf.plot_survival_function(ax=ax, ci_show=True)
plt.title('Kaplan–Meier Survival by CD274 Expression Group')
plt.xlabel('Time (days)')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
# Log-rank test
mask_high = df['CD274_group'] == 'High'
mask_low = df['CD274_group'] == 'Low'
lr = logrank_test(
    df.loc[mask_high, 'survival_time'], df.loc[mask_low, 'survival_time'],
    event_observed_A=df.loc[mask_high, 'event_observed'],
    event_observed_B=df.loc[mask_low, 'event_observed']
)
plt.text(0.6, 0.1, f'Log-rank p = {lr.p_value:.3e}', transform=ax.transAxes)
plt.show()
print(f"Log-rank test p-value: {lr.p_value:.3e}")

# 7. Cox proportional hazards model (continuous CD274 expr)
df['gender_Male'] = (df['gender'].str.upper() == 'MALE').astype(int)
cox_df = df[['survival_time', 'event_observed', 'CD274_expr', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender_Male']]
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(cox_df, duration_col='survival_time', event_col='event_observed')
print("\nCox PH model summary:")
print(cph.summary[['coef', 'exp(coef)', 'exp(coef) lower 95%', 'exp(coef) upper 95%', 'p']])

# 8. Table of results
table = df[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'CD274_expr', 'CD274_group', 'survival_time', 'event_observed']]
print(f"\nPatient-level table ({len(table)} patients):")
print(table.to_string(index=False))

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# 1. Load datasets
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Extract CD274 expression
if 'CD274' in expr.index:
    cd274 = expr.loc['CD274']
elif 'PD-L1' in expr.index:
    cd274 = expr.loc['PD-L1']
else:
    raise KeyError("CD274 not found in expression matrix index")

# 3. Map samples to patients and aggregate
patient_expr = cd274.groupby(cd274.index.str[:12]).mean()
expr_df = patient_expr.reset_index()
expr_df.columns = ['bcr_patient_barcode', 'CD274_expr']

# 4. Merge with clinical survival data
df = expr_df.merge(
    clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'vital_status', 'days_to_death', 'days_to_last_followup',
          'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender']],
    on='bcr_patient_barcode', how='inner'
)

# Compute survival time and event
# Use days_to_death if dead, else days_to_last_followup
df['event_observed'] = (df['vital_status'] == 'Dead').astype(int)
# If days_to_death is NaN for dead, drop
df['survival_time'] = np.where(
    df['event_observed'] == 1,
    df['days_to_death'],
    df['days_to_last_followup']
)
df = df.dropna(subset=['survival_time', 'CD274_expr', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender'])

# 5. Dichotomize by median expression
median_expr = df['CD274_expr'].median()
df['CD274_group'] = np.where(df['CD274_expr'] >= median_expr, 'High', 'Low')

# 6. Kaplan–Meier analysis
kmf_high = KaplanMeierFitter()
kmf_low = KaplanMeierFitter()
ix_high = df['CD274_group'] == 'High'
ix_low = df['CD274_group'] == 'Low'

plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
ax = plt.subplot(111)
kmf_high.fit(df.loc[ix_high, 'survival_time'], df.loc[ix_high, 'event_observed'], label='High CD274')
kmf_low.fit(df.loc[ix_low, 'survival_time'], df.loc[ix_low, 'event_observed'], label='Low CD274')
kmf_high.plot_survival_function(ax=ax, ci_show=True)
kmf_low.plot_survival_function(ax=ax, ci_show=True)
plt.title('Kaplan–Meier: CD274 High vs Low')
plt.xlabel('Time (days)')
plt.ylabel('Survival probability')

# Log-rank test
results = logrank_test(
    df.loc[ix_high, 'survival_time'], df.loc[ix_low, 'survival_time'],
    event_observed_A=df.loc[ix_high, 'event_observed'],
    event_observed_B=df.loc[ix_low, 'event_observed']
)
p_lr = results.p_value
plt.text(0.6, 0.1, f'Log-rank p = {p_lr:.3e}', transform=ax.transAxes)
plt.show()
print(f"Log-rank test p-value: {p_lr:.3e}")

# 7. Cox proportional hazards model
# Encode gender: Male=1, Female=0
df['gender_Male'] = (df['gender'].str.upper() == 'MALE').astype(int)
cox_df = df[['survival_time', 'event_observed', 'CD274_expr', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender_Male']]

cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(cox_df, duration_col='survival_time', event_col='event_observed')
print("\nCox PH model summary:")
print(cph.summary[['coef', 'exp(coef)', 'exp(coef) lower 95%', 'exp(coef) upper 95%', 'p']])

# 8. Output table of patient data
table = df[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'CD274_expr', 'CD274_group', 'survival_time', 'event_observed']]
print(f"\nPatient-level table ({len(table)} rows):")
print(table.to_string(index=False))"}

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# 1. Load datasets
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Locate CD274 by Ensembl ID (ENSG00000120217), handling version suffix
ens_ids = expr.index.to_series().str.split('.').str[0]
matches = ens_ids[ens_ids == 'ENSG00000120217']
if len(matches) != 1:
    raise KeyError("CD274 Ensembl ID ENSG00000120217 not found or ambiguous in expression matrix")
gene_idx = matches.index[0]
cd274_series = expr.loc[gene_idx]  # Series: sample barcodes -> expression values

# 3. Map samples to patients and compute mean if multiple samples
patient_expr = cd274_series.groupby(cd274_series.index.str[:12]).mean()
expr_df = patient_expr.rename('CD274_expr').reset_index().rename(columns={'index':'bcr_patient_barcode'})

# 4. Merge with clinical data for survival analysis
df = expr_df.merge(
    clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'vital_status', 'days_to_death', 'days_to_last_followup',
          'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender']],
    on='bcr_patient_barcode', how='inner'
)

# Compute event and survival time
df['event_observed'] = (df['vital_status'] == 'Dead').astype(int)
df['survival_time'] = np.where(
    df['event_observed'] == 1,
    df['days_to_death'],
    df['days_to_last_followup']
)
df = df.dropna(subset=['survival_time', 'CD274_expr', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender'])

# 5. Dichotomize by median CD274 expression
df['CD274_group'] = np.where(
    df['CD274_expr'] >= df['CD274_expr'].median(), 'High', 'Low'
)

# 6. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
ax = plt.subplot(111)
for label in ['High', 'Low']:
    mask = df['CD274_group'] == label
    kmf.fit(df.loc[mask, 'survival_time'], df.loc[mask, 'event_observed'], label=f'{label} CD274')
    kmf.plot_survival_function(ax=ax, ci_show=True)
plt.title('Kaplan–Meier Survival by CD274 Expression Group')
plt.xlabel('Time (days)')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
# Log-rank test
mask_high = df['CD274_group'] == 'High'
mask_low = df['CD274_group'] == 'Low'
lr = logrank_test(
    df.loc[mask_high, 'survival_time'], df.loc[mask_low, 'survival_time'],
    event_observed_A=df.loc[mask_high, 'event_observed'],
    event_observed_B=df.loc[mask_low, 'event_observed']
)
plt.text(0.6, 0.1, f'Log-rank p = {lr.p_value:.3e}', transform=ax.transAxes)
plt.show()
print(f"Log-rank test p-value: {lr.p_value:.3e}")

print("\nCox PH model summary:")

hypothesis: Patients with ulcerated primary melanomas (ulceration_indicator = YES) have higher tumor mutational burden (TMB) than those without ulceration (NO).

experiment_plan.objective: Compare somatic mutation counts between ulcerated and non‐ulcerated tumors to test if ulceration status is associated with higher TMB.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_mutations.csv.
2. From clinical data, filter to non‐missing ulceration_indicator and keep records where ulceration_indicator is 'YES' or 'NO'.
3. In the mutation dataset, count total mutations per patient_id to obtain TMB.
4. Map clinical patient barcodes (bcr_patient_barcode) to mutation patient_id and merge ulceration status with TMB.
5. Compare TMB distributions between ulceration groups using the Wilcoxon rank‐sum test (or t‐test after checking normality).
6. Fit a negative‐binomial or Poisson regression model predicting mutation_count from ulceration_indicator, adjusting for age_at_diagnosis and gender.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
1. Table of per‐patient ulceration status and mutation counts.
2. Boxplot or violin plot of TMB by ulceration status.
3. Wilcoxon test statistic and p‐value (and/or t‐test result).
4. Regression model summary with coefficient for ulceration_indicator and covariates.

code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.genmod.families import Poisson
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)

# 2. Filter clinical data for ulceration status
clin_filt = clinical[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender', 'ulceration_indicator']]\
    .dropna(subset=['ulceration_indicator'])
clin_filt = clin_filt[clin_filt['ulceration_indicator'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]

# 3. Count total mutations per patient
tmb = mutations.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='mutation_count')

# 4. Merge TMB with clinical ulceration status
data = pd.merge(clin_filt,
                tmb,
                left_on='bcr_patient_barcode',
                right_on='patient_id',
                how='inner')

# 1. Table of per-patient ulceration status and mutation counts
print("Per-patient ulceration status and mutation counts (first 10 rows):")
print(data[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'ulceration_indicator', 'mutation_count']].head(10).to_string(index=False))

# 2. Boxplot of TMB by ulceration status
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.boxplot(x='ulceration_indicator', y='mutation_count', data=data)
plt.xlabel('Ulceration Indicator')
plt.ylabel('Tumor Mutational Burden (mutation count)')
plt.title('TMB by Ulceration Status')
plt.show()

# 3. Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Mann-Whitney U)
group_yes = data.loc[data['ulceration_indicator']=='YES', 'mutation_count']
group_no  = data.loc[data['ulceration_indicator']=='NO',  'mutation_count']
st, p_value = mannwhitneyu(group_yes, group_no, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"Mann-Whitney U test: U = {st:.2f}, p-value = {p_value:.4f}")

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.genmod.families import Poisson
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)

# 2. Filter clinical data for ulceration status
clin_filt = clinical[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender', 'ulceration_indicator']]\
    .dropna(subset=['ulceration_indicator'])
clin_filt = clin_filt[clin_filt['ulceration_indicator'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]

# 3. Count total mutations per patient
tmb = mutations.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='mutation_count')

# 4. Merge TMB with clinical ulceration status
data = pd.merge(clin_filt,
                tmb,
                left_on='bcr_patient_barcode',
                right_on='patient_id',
                how='inner')

# 1. Table of per-patient ulceration status and mutation counts
print("Per-patient ulceration status and mutation counts (first 10 rows):")
print(data[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'ulceration_indicator', 'mutation_count']].head(10).to_string(index=False))

# 2. Boxplot of TMB by ulceration status
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.boxplot(x='ulceration_indicator', y='mutation_count', data=data)
plt.xlabel('Ulceration Indicator')
plt.ylabel('Tumor Mutational Burden (mutation count)')
plt.title('TMB by Ulceration Status')
plt.show()

# 3. Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Mann-Whitney U)
group_yes = data.loc[data['ulceration_indicator']=='YES', 'mutation_count']
group_no  = data.loc[data['ulceration_indicator']=='NO',  'mutation_count']
st, p_value = mannwhitneyu(group_yes, group_no, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"Mann-Whitney U test: U = {st:.2f}, p-value = {p_value:.4f}")

# 4. Poisson regression predicting mutation_count from ulceration, age, and gender
#    Encode categorical variables
model = smf.glm(
    formula='mutation_count ~ C(ulceration_indicator) + age_at_diagnosis + C(gender)',
    data=data,
    family=Poisson()
).fit()
print("\nPoisson regression summary:")
print(model.summary())"}

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# Load clinical data
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
# Select relevant columns
clin = clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'ethnicity', 'age_at_diagnosis',
             'days_to_death', 'days_to_last_followup', 'vital_status']]
# Filter missing in key covariates (keep death/followup for later)
clin = clin.dropna(subset=['ethnicity', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'vital_status'])
# Filter ethnicity groups
clin = clin[clin['ethnicity'].isin(['HISPANIC OR LATINO', 'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO'])]
clin['ethnicity_group'] = clin['ethnicity'].map({
    'HISPANIC OR LATINO': 'Hispanic',
    'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO': 'Non-Hispanic'
})
# Define survival time and event
clin['time'] = clin['days_to_death'].fillna(clin['days_to_last_followup'])
clin['event'] = (clin['vital_status'] == 'Dead').astype(int)
# Drop rows with missing time
clin = clin.dropna(subset=['time'])

# Report patient counts
print("Patient counts by ethnicity group:")
print(clin['ethnicity_group'].value_counts(), "\n")

# Kaplan-Meier curves
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
for grp in ['Hispanic', 'Non-Hispanic']:
    mask = clin['ethnicity_group'] == grp
    kmf.fit(clin.loc[mask, 'time'], event_observed=clin.loc[mask, 'event'], label=grp)
    kmf.plot(ci_show=True)
plt.title('Kaplan-Meier Survival by Ethnicity')
plt.xlabel('Days')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Log-rank test
lr = logrank_test(
    clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Hispanic', 'time'],
    clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Non-Hispanic', 'time'],
    event_observed_A=clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Hispanic', 'event'],
    event_observed_B=clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Non-Hispanic', 'event']
)
print(f"Log-rank test p-value: {lr.p_value:.4f}\n")

# Cox proportional hazards model (excluding stage)
df_cox = clin[['time', 'event', 'age_at_diagnosis']].copy()
df_cox['ethnicity_Hispanic'] = (clin['ethnicity_group'] == 'Hispanic').astype(int)
# Fit Cox model
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(df_cox, duration_col='time', event_col='event')
print("Cox model summary:")
print(cph.summary[['coef', 'exp(coef)', 'exp(coef) lower 95%', 'exp(coef) upper 95%', 'p']])

# Check proportional hazards assumption
print("\nProportional hazards assumption check:")
cph.check_assumptions(df_cox, p_value_threshold=0.05, show_plots=False)

# Forest plot of hazard ratios
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
cph.plot(hazard_ratios=True)
plt.title('Hazard Ratios')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Patients with Clark level IV and V exhibit a higher somatic tumor mutational burden (TMB) compared to those with levels I–III, after adjusting for age and gender.

4. From cleaned_mutations.csv, count total mutations per patient_id as TMB.  
5. Merge TMB per patient with clinical subset on patient barcode.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Melanoma patients with high baseline Breslow thickness have a distinct immunomodulatory gene expression profile compared to those with low thickness.

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# Step 1: Load clinical data
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')

# Define ethnicity groups and filter
clin = clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'ethnicity', 'age_at_diagnosis',
             'ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw', 'days_to_death', 'days_to_last_followup', 'vital_status']]
clin = clin.dropna(subset=['ethnicity', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw'])
clin = clin[clin['ethnicity'].isin(['HISPANIC OR LATINO', 'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO'])]
clin['ethnicity_group'] = clin['ethnicity'].map({
    'HISPANIC OR LATINO': 'Hispanic',
    'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO': 'Non-Hispanic'
})

# Step 2: Define survival time and event
clin['time'] = np.where(clin['days_to_death'].notna(),
                         clin['days_to_death'],
                         clin['days_to_last_followup'])
clin['event'] = (clin['vital_status'] == 'Dead').astype(int)

# Drop any remaining missing
clin = clin.dropna(subset=['time', 'event'])

# Report group counts
counts = clin['ethnicity_group'].value_counts()
print("Patient counts by ethnicity group:")
print(counts, "\n")

# Step 3: Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank test
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
for group in ['Hispanic', 'Non-Hispanic']:
    mask = clin['ethnicity_group'] == group
    kmf.fit(clin.loc[mask, 'time'], event_observed=clin.loc[mask, 'event'], label=group)
    kmf.plot(ci_show=True)

plt.title('Kaplan-Meier Survival by Ethnicity')
plt.xlabel('Days')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Log-rank test
test = logrank_test(
    clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Hispanic', 'time'],
    clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Non-Hispanic', 'time'],
    event_observed_A=clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Hispanic', 'event'],
    event_observed_B=clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Non-Hispanic', 'event']
)
print(f"Log-rank test p-value: {test.p_value:.4f}\n")

# Step 4: Cox proportional hazards model
# Prepare data for Cox model
df_cox = clin[['time', 'event', 'ethnicity_group', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw']].copy()
# Encode ethnicity_binary
df_cox['ethnicity_Hispanic'] = (df_cox['ethnicity_group']=='Hispanic').astype(int)
# One-hot encode AJCC stage
stage_dummies = pd.get_dummies(df_cox['ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw'], prefix='stage', drop_first=True)
df_cox = pd.concat([df_cox.drop(columns=['ethnicity_group','ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw']), stage_dummies], axis=1)

# Fit Cox model
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(df_cox, duration_col='time', event_col='event', show_progress=False)
print("Cox model summary:")
print(cph.summary[['coef', 'exp(coef)', 'exp(coef) lower 95%', 'exp(coef) upper 95%', 'p']])

# Check proportional hazards assumption
print("\nChecking proportional hazards assumptions:")
cph.check_assumptions(df_cox, p_value_threshold=0.05, show_plots=False)

# Optional: forest plot of hazard ratios
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
cph.plot(hazard_ratios=True)
plt.title('Hazard Ratios from Cox Model')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()"}

import numpy as np

from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# Load clinical data
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')

# Ensure AJCC stage column exists; use 'ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw' fallback if present
if 'ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw' not in clin.columns:
    raise KeyError("AJCC pathologic stage data not found in clinical dataset. Column 'ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw' is missing.")

stage_col = 'ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw'

# Select relevant columns
clin = clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'ethnicity', 'age_at_diagnosis',
             stage_col, 'days_to_death', 'days_to_last_followup', 'vital_status']]

# Define and filter ethnicity groups
clin = clin.dropna(subset=['ethnicity', 'age_at_diagnosis', stage_col])
clin = clin[clin['ethnicity'].isin(['HISPANIC OR LATINO', 'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO'])]
clin['ethnicity_group'] = clin['ethnicity'].map({
    'HISPANIC OR LATINO': 'Hispanic',
    'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO': 'Non-Hispanic'
})

# Define survival time and event
clin['time'] = np.where(clin['days_to_death'].notna(),
                         clin['days_to_death'],
                         clin['days_to_last_followup'])
clin['event'] = (clin['vital_status'] == 'Dead').astype(int)
clin = clin.dropna(subset=['time', 'event'])

# Check patient counts
print("Patient counts by ethnicity:")
print(clin['ethnicity_group'].value_counts(), "\n")

# Kaplan-Meier curves
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
for grp in ['Hispanic', 'Non-Hispanic']:
    mask = clin['ethnicity_group'] == grp
    kmf.fit(clin.loc[mask, 'time'], event_observed=clin.loc[mask, 'event'], label=grp)
    kmf.plot(ci_show=True)

plt.tight_layout()

    clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Hispanic', 'time'],
    clin.loc[clin['ethnicity_group']=='Non-Hispanic', 'time'],

)

# Prepare Cox model data

df_cox = pd.concat([df_cox.drop(columns=['ethnicity_group', stage_col]), staged], axis=1)

# Fit Cox model
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(df_cox, duration_col='time', event_col='event')
print("Cox model summary:")
print(cph.summary[['coef','exp(coef)','exp(coef) lower 95%','exp(coef) upper 95%','p']])

# Check PH assumption
print("\nProportional hazards assumption check:")
cph.check_assumptions(df_cox, p_value_threshold=0.05, show_plots=False)

hypothesis: Body mass index (BMI) at diagnosis is inversely correlated with tumor mutational burden in melanoma patients.

experiment_plan.objective: Test the association between BMI and total somatic mutation counts.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_mutations.csv.  2. Filter clinical data for non‐missing height_cm and weight_kg.  3. Compute BMI = weight_kg / (height_cm/100)^2.  4. Count total somatic mutations per patient.  5. Merge BMI and mutation counts by patient ID.  6. Compute Spearman correlation between BMI and mutation count.  7. Fit a linear model (or Poisson regression) predicting mutation count from BMI, adjust for age_at_diagnosis and gender.  8. Produce scatter plot of BMI vs mutation count with regression line.
experiment_plan.deliverables: • Spearman ρ and p‐value.  • Regression model summary with BMI coefficient.  • Scatter plot with fitted regression curve.  • Table of patient‐level BMI and mutation counts.

code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Load datasets
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# 2. Filter for non-missing height and weight
clinical = clinical.dropna(subset=['height_cm', 'weight_kg', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender'])

# 3. Compute BMI
clinical['BMI'] = clinical['weight_kg'] / (clinical['height_cm'] / 100) ** 2

# 4. Count total somatic mutations per patient
mut_counts = mutations.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='mutation_count')

# 5. Merge BMI and mutation counts
# clinical submitter_id matches mutations patient_id
df = pd.merge(clinical, mut_counts, left_on='submitter_id', right_on='patient_id', how='inner')
print(f"Merged data: {len(df)} patients with BMI and mutation counts")
print(df[['submitter_id', 'BMI', 'mutation_count']].head(10))

# 6. Spearman correlation
rho, pval = spearmanr(df['BMI'], df['mutation_count'])
print(f"Spearman correlation between BMI and mutation count: rho = {rho:.3f}, p-value = {pval:.3e}")

# 7. Regression: linear model on log-transformed mutation count adjusting for age and gender
df['log_mut_count'] = np.log1p(df['mutation_count'])
model = smf.ols('log_mut_count ~ BMI + age_at_diagnosis + C(gender)', data=df).fit()
print(model.summary())

# 8. Scatter plot with regression line
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.regplot(x='BMI', y='mutation_count', data=df,
            scatter_kws={'alpha':0.5, 's':30}, line_kws={'color':'red'})
plt.xlabel('BMI at Diagnosis')
plt.ylabel('Total Somatic Mutation Count')
plt.title('BMI vs Tumor Mutation Burden with Fitted Regression Line')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Load datasets
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# 2. Filter for non-missing height and weight
clinical = clinical.dropna(subset=['height_cm', 'weight_kg', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender'])

# 3. Compute BMI
clinical['BMI'] = clinical['weight_kg'] / (clinical['height_cm'] / 100) ** 2

# 4. Count total somatic mutations per patient
mut_counts = mutations.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='mutation_count')

# 5. Merge BMI and mutation counts
# clinical submitter_id matches mutations patient_id
df = pd.merge(clinical, mut_counts, left_on='submitter_id', right_on='patient_id', how='inner')
print(f"Merged data: {len(df)} patients with BMI and mutation counts")
print(df[['submitter_id', 'BMI', 'mutation_count']].head(10))

# 6. Spearman correlation
rho, pval = spearmanr(df['BMI'], df['mutation_count'])
print(f"Spearman correlation between BMI and mutation count: rho = {rho:.3f}, p-value = {pval:.3e}")

# 7. Regression: linear model on log-transformed mutation count adjusting for age and gender
df['log_mut_count'] = np.log1p(df['mutation_count'])
model = smf.ols('log_mut_count ~ BMI + age_at_diagnosis + C(gender)', data=df).fit()
print(model.summary())

# 8. Scatter plot with regression line
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.regplot(x='BMI', y='mutation_count', data=df,
            scatter_kws={'alpha':0.5, 's':30}, line_kws={'color':'red'})
plt.xlabel('BMI at Diagnosis')
plt.ylabel('Total Somatic Mutation Count')
plt.title('BMI vs Tumor Mutation Burden with Fitted Regression Line')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()"}

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu, ttest_ind
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

# 1. Load datasets
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)
# Strip version suffix from Ensembl IDs
expr.index = expr.index.str.split('.').str[0]

# 2. Compute per-patient TMB
tmb = mutations.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='TMB')
tmb.rename(columns={'patient_id': 'bcr_patient_barcode'}, inplace=True)

# 3. Subset clinical by ethnicity and merge TMB
eth_groups = ['HISPANIC OR LATINO', 'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO']
clin_sub = clinical[clinical['ethnicity'].isin(eth_groups)][
    ['bcr_patient_barcode', 'ethnicity']].drop_duplicates()
clin_sub = clin_sub.merge(tmb, on='bcr_patient_barcode', how='left').fillna({'TMB': 0})

# 4. Mann–Whitney U test for TMB by ethnicity
g1 = clin_sub[clin_sub['ethnicity']=='HISPANIC OR LATINO']['TMB']
g2 = clin_sub[clin_sub['ethnicity']=='NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO']['TMB']
u_stat, p_tmb = mannwhitneyu(g1, g2, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"Mann–Whitney U test for TMB by ethnicity: U = {u_stat:.2f}, p = {p_tmb:.3e}\n")

# Boxplot of TMB
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
sns.boxplot(x='ethnicity', y='TMB', data=clin_sub, hue='ethnicity', dodge=False, palette=['blue','red'], legend=False)
plt.xticks(rotation=30)
plt.title('TMB by Ethnicity')
plt.xlabel('Ethnicity')
plt.ylabel('Tumor Mutational Burden')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 5. Map immune gene symbols to Ensembl IDs without version
# Manual mapping for common genes
gene_map = {
    'CD8A': 'ENSG00000153563',
    'PDCD1': 'ENSG00000188389',
    'CD274': 'ENSG00000120217',
    'CTLA4': 'ENSG00000163599',
    'LAG3': 'ENSG00000089605'
}
# Filter to those present in expr index
mapped = {g: eid for g, eid in gene_map.items() if eid in expr.index}
if not mapped:
    raise ValueError('None of the immune gene Ensembl IDs found in expression data.')

# 6. Prepare expression data for immune genes
expr.columns = expr.columns.str.slice(0, 12)
samples = clin_sub['bcr_patient_barcode'].tolist()
avail = [s for s in samples if s in expr.columns]
expr_sub = expr[avail]
expr_imm = expr_sub.loc[list(mapped.values())]
expr_imm.index = list(mapped.keys())  # rename to gene symbols
expr_imm = expr_imm.transpose()
expr_imm['ethnicity'] = clin_sub.set_index('bcr_patient_barcode').loc[expr_imm.index, 'ethnicity']

# Differential expression tests for immune genes
results = []
for gene in mapped.keys():
    grp1 = expr_imm[expr_imm['ethnicity']=='HISPANIC OR LATINO'][gene]
    grp2 = expr_imm[expr_imm['ethnicity']=='NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO'][gene]
    stat, pval = ttest_ind(grp1, grp2, nan_policy='omit')
    logfc = grp1.mean() - grp2.mean()
    results.append({'gene': gene, 'log2FC': logfc, 'p-value': pval})
df_res = pd.DataFrame(results).set_index('gene')
df_res['adj_p'] = multipletests(df_res['p-value'], method='fdr_bh')[1]
print('Immune gene differential expression results:')
print(df_res, '\n')

# 7. Heatmap of immune gene expression
heat = expr_imm.drop(columns='ethnicity').apply(lambda x: (x - x.mean())/x.std(), axis=0)
eth_map = {'HISPANIC OR LATINO':'red', 'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO':'blue'}
col_colors = expr_imm['ethnicity'].map(eth_map)

sns.clustermap(heat.transpose(), col_cluster=False, row_cluster=False,
               col_colors=col_colors, cmap='vlag', figsize=(6,4))
plt.suptitle('Immune Gene Expression Heatmap (z-score)', y=1.05)
plt.show()

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu, ttest_ind, zscore
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

# 1. Load datasets
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Compute per-patient TMB
# Count mutations per patient_id
tmb = mutations.groupby('patient_id').size().reset_index(name='TMB')
tmb.rename(columns={'patient_id': 'bcr_patient_barcode'}, inplace=True)

# 3. Subset clinical by ethnicity and merge TMB
eth_groups = ['HISPANIC OR LATINO', 'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO']
clin_sub = clinical[clinical['ethnicity'].isin(eth_groups)][[
    'bcr_patient_barcode', 'ethnicity']].drop_duplicates()
clin_sub = clin_sub.merge(tmb, on='bcr_patient_barcode', how='left').fillna({'TMB': 0})

# 4. Mann–Whitney U test for TMB by ethnicity
g1 = clin_sub[clin_sub['ethnicity']=='HISPANIC OR LATINO']['TMB']
g2 = clin_sub[clin_sub['ethnicity']=='NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO']['TMB']
u_stat, p_tmb = mannwhitneyu(g1, g2, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"Mann–Whitney U test for TMB by ethnicity: U = {u_stat:.2f}, p = {p_tmb:.3e}")

# Boxplot of TMB
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
sns.boxplot(x='ethnicity', y='TMB', data=clin_sub, palette=['red','blue'])
plt.xticks(rotation=30)
plt.title('TMB by Ethnicity')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 5. Extract immune-related genes
immune_genes = ['CD8A', 'PDCD1', 'CD274', 'CTLA4', 'LAG3']
# Align expression columns to patient barcodes (first 12 chars)
expr.columns = expr.columns.str.slice(0, 12)
# Select samples present in clin_sub
samples = [s for s in clin_sub['bcr_patient_barcode'] if s in expr.columns]
expr_sub = expr[samples]

# 6. Compare expression for immune genes
# Subset immune genes
expr_immune = expr_sub.loc[expr_sub.index.intersection(immune_genes)].copy()
expr_immune = expr_immune.transpose()  # samples x genes
# Align with clinical
expr_immune['ethnicity'] = clin_sub.set_index('bcr_patient_barcode').loc[expr_immune.index, 'ethnicity']

results = []
for gene in immune_genes:
    if gene in expr_immune.columns:
        grp1 = expr_immune[expr_immune['ethnicity']=='HISPANIC OR LATINO'][gene]
        grp2 = expr_immune[expr_immune['ethnicity']=='NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO'][gene]
        stat, pval = ttest_ind(grp1, grp2, nan_policy='omit')
        logfc = grp1.mean() - grp2.mean()
        results.append({'gene': gene, 'log2FC': logfc, 'p-value': pval})

df_res = pd.DataFrame(results).set_index('gene')
# Adjust p-values
df_res['adj_p'] = multipletests(df_res['p-value'], method='fdr_bh')[1]
print("\nImmune gene differential expression results:")
print(df_res)

# 7. Heatmap of immune gene expression (z-scored per gene)
# Prepare data matrix
heat_data = expr_immune[expr_immune.columns.intersection(immune_genes)]
heat_z = heat_data.apply(zscore, axis=0).transpose()
# Column colors by ethnicity
eth_map = {'HISPANIC OR LATINO':'red', 'NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO':'blue'}
col_colors = expr_immune['ethnicity'].map(eth_map)

sns.clustermap(heat_z, col_cluster=False, row_cluster=False,
               col_colors=col_colors, cmap='vlag', figsize=(6,4))
plt.suptitle('Heatmap of Immune Gene Expression (z-score)', y=1.05)
plt.show()"}

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import spearmanr, mannwhitneyu
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', usecols=['bcr_patient_barcode'])
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)
mut = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# 2. Compute TMB (mutations per patient)
tmb = mut.groupby('patient_id').size().rename('TMB').reset_index()
# include patients with zero mutations
all_patients = pd.DataFrame({'patient_id': clinical['bcr_patient_barcode'].unique()})
tmb = all_patients.merge(tmb, on='patient_id', how='left').fillna(0)

# 3. Map samples to patients for expression
samples = expr.columns.tolist()
patient_ids = [s[:12] for s in samples]

# 4. Immune checkpoint genes and mapping to Ensembl IDs
genes = ['PDCD1', 'CD274', 'CTLA4', 'LAG3', 'TIGIT']
try:
    import mygene
except ImportError:
    import subprocess, sys
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', 'mygene'])
    import mygene
mg = mygene.MyGeneInfo()
res = mg.querymany(genes, scopes='symbol', fields='ensembl.gene', species='human')
# extract Ensembl IDs
ensembl_ids = []
for r in res:
    gene_info = r.get('ensembl')
    if isinstance(gene_info, list):
        en = gene_info[0].get('gene')
    elif isinstance(gene_info, dict):
        en = gene_info.get('gene')
    else:
        en = None
    if en:
        # match prefix ignoring version
        if en not in ensembl_ids:
            ensembl_ids.append(en)

# 5. Extract expression rows for these genes
mask = expr.index.to_series().apply(lambda x: any(x.startswith(e) for e in ensembl_ids))
imm_expr = expr[mask]

# 6. Compute immune checkpoint score per sample (mean expression)
immune_scores = imm_expr.mean(axis=0)
immune_df = pd.DataFrame({'sample': immune_scores.index, 'immune_score': immune_scores.values})
immune_df['patient_id'] = immune_df['sample'].str[:12]

# 7. Merge TMB with immune scores per patient
df = tmb.merge(immune_df.groupby('patient_id')['immune_score'].mean().reset_index(), on='patient_id', how='inner')

# 8. Spearman correlation
rho, p_spearman = spearmanr(df['TMB'], df['immune_score'])

# 9. Dichotomize by median TMB and Wilcoxon test

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import spearmanr, mannwhitneyu
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', usecols=['bcr_patient_barcode'])
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)
mut = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# 2. Compute TMB (mutations per patient)
tmb = mut.groupby('patient_id').size().rename('TMB').reset_index()
# include patients with zero mutations
all_patients = pd.DataFrame({'patient_id': clinical['bcr_patient_barcode'].unique()})
tmb = all_patients.merge(tmb, on='patient_id', how='left').fillna(0)

# 3. Map samples to patients for expression
samples = expr.columns.tolist()
patient_ids = [s[:12] for s in samples]

# 4. Immune checkpoint genes and mapping to Ensembl IDs
genes = ['PDCD1', 'CD274', 'CTLA4', 'LAG3', 'TIGIT']
try:
    import mygene
except ImportError:
    import subprocess, sys
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', 'mygene'])
    import mygene
mg = mygene.MyGeneInfo()
res = mg.querymany(genes, scopes='symbol', fields='ensembl.gene', species='human')
# extract Ensembl IDs
ensembl_ids = []
for r in res:
    gene_info = r.get('ensembl')
    if isinstance(gene_info, list):
        en = gene_info[0].get('gene')
    elif isinstance(gene_info, dict):
        en = gene_info.get('gene')
    else:
        en = None
    if en:
        # match prefix ignoring version
        if en not in ensembl_ids:
            ensembl_ids.append(en)

# 5. Extract expression rows for these genes
mask = expr.index.to_series().apply(lambda x: any(x.startswith(e) for e in ensembl_ids))
imm_expr = expr[mask]

# 6. Compute immune checkpoint score per sample (mean expression)
immune_scores = imm_expr.mean(axis=0)
immune_df = pd.DataFrame({'sample': immune_scores.index, 'immune_score': immune_scores.values})
immune_df['patient_id'] = immune_df['sample'].str[:12]

# 7. Merge TMB with immune scores per patient
df = tmb.merge(immune_df.groupby('patient_id')['immune_score'].mean().reset_index(), on='patient_id', how='inner')

# 8. Spearman correlation
rho, p_spearman = spearmanr(df['TMB'], df['immune_score'])

# 9. Dichotomize by median TMB and Wilcoxon test
median_tmb = df['TMB'].median()
df['TMB_group'] = np.where(df['TMB'] >= median_tmb, 'High', 'Low')
g1 = df.loc[df['TMB_group']=='High', 'immune_score']
g2 = df.loc[df['TMB_group']=='Low', 'immune_score']
stat_w, p_w = mannwhitneyu(g1, g2, alternative='two-sided')

# 10. Outputs
print(f"Number of patients with both TMB and immune scores: {len(df)}")
print(f"Spearman correlation: rho = {rho:.3f}, p-value = {p_spearman:.3g}")
print(f"Wilcoxon rank-sum test (High vs Low TMB): statistic = {stat_w:.3f}, p-value = {p_w:.3g}")
print("\nSample of patient-level results:")
print(df[['patient_id','TMB','immune_score','TMB_group']].head(), "\n")

# 11. Visualizations
plt.figure(figsize=(6,5))
plt.scatter(df['TMB'], df['immune_score'], alpha=0.7)
# regression line
a = np.polyfit(df['TMB'], df['immune_score'], 1)
plt.plot(df['TMB'], np.polyval(a, df['TMB']), color='red', lw=1)
plt.xlabel('Tumor Mutational Burden')
plt.ylabel('Immune Checkpoint Score')
plt.title(f'Scatter: TMB vs Immune Score\nSpearman rho={rho:.2f}, p={p_spearman:.3g}')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

plt.figure(figsize=(6,5))
import seaborn as sns
sns.boxplot(x='TMB_group', y='immune_score', data=df, palette='Set2')
plt.xlabel('TMB Group')
plt.ylabel('Immune Checkpoint Score')
plt.title('Immune Score by TMB Group\nWilcoxon p=' + f"{p_w:.3g}")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()"}

1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv.  
2. Subset to patients with non-missing mitotic_count_per_mm2 and clinical survival data.  
3. Define a cell cycle gene signature (e.g., CCNB1, CDK1, MCM2).  
4. Compute a cell cycle score per tumor using average expression or GSVA.  
5. Correlate mitotic_count_per_mm2 with cell cycle score using Spearman correlation and fit a linear model adjusting for age_at_diagnosis and gender.  
6. Divide patients into high vs low mitotic_count by median.  
7. Fit Kaplan–Meier curves and log-rank test comparing high vs low groups.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test
import subprocess, sys

def install(pkg): subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', pkg])
try:
    import mygene
except ImportError:
    install('mygene')
    import mygene

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# Strip Ensembl version suffix
expr.index = expr.index.str.split('.').str[0]
# Map samples to patients
expr.columns = expr.columns.str[:12]
expr_agg = expr.T.groupby(expr.columns).mean().T

# 2. Clinical survival and subset
clinical['survival_time'] = np.where(
    clinical['vital_status']=='Dead', clinical['days_to_death'], clinical['days_to_last_followup'])
clinical['event'] = (clinical['vital_status']=='Dead').astype(int)
clinical_sub = clinical.dropna(subset=['mitotic_count_per_mm2','survival_time','age_at_diagnosis','gender'])
clinical_sub = clinical_sub.set_index('bcr_patient_barcode')
common = clinical_sub.index.intersection(expr_agg.columns)
clinical_sub = clinical_sub.loc[common]
expr_agg = expr_agg[common]

# 3. Map signature genes to Ensembl
signature = ['CCNB1','CDK1','MCM2']
mg = mygene.MyGeneInfo()
res = mg.querymany(signature, scopes='symbol', fields='ensembl.gene', species='human')
sym2ens = {}
for r in res:
    q = r['query']
    eg = r.get('ensembl')
    if isinstance(eg,list): sym2ens[q] = [e['gene'] for e in eg if 'gene' in e]
    elif isinstance(eg,dict) and 'gene' in eg: sym2ens[q] = [eg['gene']]
ens_ids = [e for lst in sym2ens.values() for e in lst]
genes_present = [e for e in ens_ids if e in expr_agg.index]
if not genes_present:
    raise ValueError(f"No signature genes found; mapped IDs: {ens_ids}")

# 4. Compute cell cycle score
cc_score = expr_agg.loc[genes_present].T.mean(axis=1)
clinical_sub['cell_cycle_score'] = cc_score

# 5. Correlation & regression
rho,p = spearmanr(clinical_sub['mitotic_count_per_mm2'], clinical_sub['cell_cycle_score'])
print(f"Spearman rho={rho:.3f}, p={p:.3g}")
lm = smf.ols('cell_cycle_score ~ mitotic_count_per_mm2 + age_at_diagnosis + C(gender)', data=clinical_sub.reset_index()).fit()
print(lm.summary())

# 6. KM by mitotic count group
med = clinical_sub['mitotic_count_per_mm2'].median()
clinical_sub['mitotic_group'] = np.where(clinical_sub['mitotic_count_per_mm2']>=med,'High','Low')
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
for grp,ls in [('Low','-'),('High','--')]:
    mask = clinical_sub['mitotic_group']==grp
    kmf.fit(clinical_sub.loc[mask,'survival_time'], clinical_sub.loc[mask,'event'], label=grp)
    kmf.plot_survival_function(ci_show=True, linestyle=ls)
plt.title('KM by Mitotic Count')
plt.xlabel('Days')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
plt.show()
res = logrank_test(
    clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub['mitotic_group']=='Low','survival_time'],
    clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub['mitotic_group']=='High','survival_time'],
    event_observed_A=clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub['mitotic_group']=='Low','event'],
    event_observed_B=clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub['mitotic_group']=='High','event'])
print(f"Log-rank chi2={res.test_statistic:.3f}, p={res.p_value:.3g}")

# 7. Cox model
clinical_sub['gender_num'] = (clinical_sub['gender']=='MALE').astype(int)
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(clinical_sub[['survival_time','event','mitotic_count_per_mm2','cell_cycle_score','age_at_diagnosis','gender_num']], duration_col='survival_time', event_col='event')
print(cph.summary)

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) at diagnosis predicts poorer overall survival in melanoma patients.

experiment_plan.objective: Assess whether baseline NLR, derived from hemogram data, is an independent prognostic factor for overall survival.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Confirm availability of neutrophil_count and lymphocyte_count in clinical data; drop patients lacking both.
2. Compute NLR = neutrophil_count / lymphocyte_count; add a small constant to denominator to avoid division by zero.
3. Merge NLR with survival time (days_to_death or days_to_last_followup) and event (vital_status).
4. Log-transform NLR for normalization; inspect distribution and, if appropriate, categorize into tertiles.
5. Fit Cox proportional hazards model with continuous log(NLR) adjusting for age_at_diagnosis, gender, and AJCC pathologic stage (ajcc_pathologic_stage_raw).
6. Plot Kaplan–Meier curves comparing high vs low NLR tertiles; perform log-rank test.
7. Evaluate model assumptions (proportional hazards) and report hazard ratios, confidence intervals, and p-values.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Distribution plot of NLR (histogram/density).
• Cox model summary (HR, 95% CI, p-value for log(NLR)).
• KM curves for high vs low NLR tertiles and log-rank test result.
• PH assumption diagnostic (Schoenfeld residuals).

• KM plots for high vs low mitotic count and log-rank p-value.  
• Cox model summary for continuous mitotic count and cell cycle score.

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Subset clinical data
# Define survival time and event
clinical['survival_time'] = np.where(
    clinical.vital_status == 'Dead', clinical.days_to_death, clinical.days_to_last_followup)
clinical['event'] = (clinical.vital_status == 'Dead').astype(int)
# Filter for non-missing data
clinical_sub = clinical.dropna(subset=['mitotic_count_per_mm2', 'survival_time', 'age_at_diagnosis', 'gender'])
# 3. Prepare expression: collapse samples to patient-level by mean
expr.columns = [c[:12] for c in expr.columns]
expr_mean = expr.groupby(expr.columns, axis=1).mean()
# Match patients
common = clinical_sub.bcr_patient_barcode.intersection(expr_mean.columns)
clinical_sub = clinical_sub.set_index('bcr_patient_barcode').loc[common]
expr_mean = expr_mean[common]

# 4. Define cell cycle signature and compute score
signature = ['CCNB1', 'CDK1', 'MCM2']
genes_present = [g for g in signature if g in expr_mean.index]
if not genes_present:
    raise ValueError('None of the signature genes found in expression data.')
cc_expr = expr_mean.loc[genes_present].T
clinical_sub['cell_cycle_score'] = cc_expr.mean(axis=1)

# 5. Correlation and linear model
rho, pval_corr = spearmanr(clinical_sub['mitotic_count_per_mm2'], clinical_sub['cell_cycle_score'])
print(f"Spearman correlation: rho={rho:.3f}, p-value={pval_corr:.3g}")
# Linear regression adjusting for age and gender
df_lm = clinical_sub.reset_index()
model = smf.ols('cell_cycle_score ~ mitotic_count_per_mm2 + age_at_diagnosis + C(gender)', data=df_lm).fit()
print(model.summary())

# 6. Dichotomize mitotic count at median
median_mit = clinical_sub['mitotic_count_per_mm2'].median()
clinical_sub['mitotic_group'] = np.where(clinical_sub['mitotic_count_per_mm2'] >= median_mit, 'High', 'Low')

# 7. Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank test
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
for grp, style in zip(['Low', 'High'], ['-','--']):
    mask = clinical_sub['mitotic_group'] == grp
    kmf.fit(clinical_sub.loc[mask, 'survival_time'], event_observed=clinical_sub.loc[mask, 'event'], label=grp)
    kmf.plot_survival_function(ci_show=True, linestyle=style)
plt.title('KM curves by mitotic count group')
plt.xlabel('Days')
plt.ylabel('Survival probability')
plt.show()
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test
T_low = clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub.mitotic_group=='Low', 'survival_time']
E_low = clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub.mitotic_group=='Low', 'event']
T_high = clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub.mitotic_group=='High', 'survival_time']
E_high = clinical_sub.loc[clinical_sub.mitotic_group=='High', 'event']
lr = logrank_test(T_low, T_high, event_observed_A=E_low, event_observed_B=E_high)
print(f"Log-rank test: chi2={lr.test_statistic:.3f}, p-value={lr.p_value:.3g}")

# 8. Cox proportional hazards model
# Encode gender
clinical_sub['gender_numeric'] = (clinical_sub['gender'] == 'MALE').astype(int)
cph_df = clinical_sub[['survival_time','event','mitotic_count_per_mm2','cell_cycle_score','age_at_diagnosis','gender_numeric']]
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(cph_df, duration_col='survival_time', event_col='event')
print(cph.summary)
"}
